record.what_it_does: Team chat platform with channels, DMs, files, canvases, and workflows.
record.auth_notes: OAuth v2 (oauth.v2.access) issues bot (xoxb) and user (xoxp) tokens. The docs say "OAuth tokens do not expire" unless you opt into token rotation, which adds refresh tokens. Tokens should go in the Authorization: Bearer header, and that header is required for JSON write methods. A legacy `token` form parameter is also accepted, but it is the same token sent a different way. Socket Mode uses app-level tokens (xapp). Signing-secret verification is only for inbound requests, so it is not an auth method for calling the API. The MCP server uses confidential OAuth (client ID and secret), with PKCE for desktop clients.
record.access_notes: Anyone can create an app and install it with OAuth at no cost. Unlisted distribution needs no Marketplace review, but workspace admins may require approval before an app is installed. Slack recommends Marketplace listing, which is reviewed, for commercial distribution. Commercially distributed non-Marketplace apps are limited on conversations.history and conversations.replies: 1 request/min, with a maximum of 15 objects per call. This applies to apps created after 2025-05-29 and to new installs. Internal customer-built apps are exempt. The official MCP server accepts only Marketplace-published or internal apps; unlisted apps are prohibited. The free Developer Program provides sandbox Enterprise orgs.
record.api_breadth_notes: The Web API has "over 200 methods" in HTTP RPC style, not strict REST. They cover chat, conversations, users, files, reactions, search, canvases, admin, and more. The Events API pushes events over HTTP, and Socket Mode delivers them over WebSocket.
record.mcp_notes: The server is at https://mcp.slack.com/mcp and uses JSON-RPC 2.0 over Streamable HTTP. SSE and Dynamic Client Registration are not supported. Auth is confidential OAuth with client ID and secret, with PKCE for desktop clients. Only Marketplace-published and internal apps can use it; unlisted apps are prohibited.
record.blocker_notes: A self-serve OAuth app can be built today with a broad Web API and the Events API. However, a commercially distributed app outside the Marketplace gets 1 req/min and 15 objects on conversations.history and conversations.replies. That cripples message-reading tools. Using the official MCP server also requires Marketplace listing. To work at full capacity in production, the app needs Marketplace review.
